screen_decision: Retain as a high-priority human-factors/reliance study directly adjacent to explanation reliability. The evidence is mixed: heatmaps mitigate some confidence-weighted harms on deliberately erroneous detector cases, yet score+heatmap users report higher reliance; the raw-accuracy score-only vs heatmap contrast and correct-override contrast are not statistically significant. Do not cite this thesis as validation that Grad-CAM++ explanations identify true forgery evidence.
screen_reason: This is direct evidence about human decision behavior and reliance when shown a deepfake detector score plus one visualization, not a test of intrinsic explanation truth or causal faithfulness. It reports no independent artifact/region ground-truth comparison, parameter-randomization test, deletion/insertion test, or counterfactual validation of Grad-CAM++ maps. The participant sample was demographically imbalanced (predominantly young, male, technically educated); the study was an online questionnaire; it used only FaceForensics++ and Grad-CAM++; and the authors note its 60-image, uniformly distributed-score, 50%-AI-error design may not match real-world detector performance. A self-reported reliance item is not equivalent to trial-level appropriate-reliance calibration.
screen_basis: Official VUT PDF text, targeted sections 5.1, 6.1, 6.3, 6.5 and 6.6; no duplicate Scholar pages or bibliography positions were rescreened.
